results.title: The prime catalogue
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $W\ge1$, $k\ge0$ and $B\ge0$ be integers. For each residue $r$ with $1\le r<W$ and $\gcd(r,W)=1$, let $p_{r,1}<p_{r,2}<\dots<p_{r,k}$ be the first $k$ primes $p$ with $p>B$ and $p\equiv r\pmod W$. Define \mathrm{catalogue\_max}(W,k,B)=\max_{r,j}p_{r,j},$$ with the maximum of an empty family equal to $0$. The fixed catalogue of the manuscript is $W=4\prod_{p\le324}p$, $k=22$, $B=324$: the first twenty-two primes…

results.title: The least formal multiple
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Every $u\in K_0$ has a unique normalized representation $u=(a+bs)/c$ with $a,b,c\in\mathbb Z$, $c>0$ and $\gcd(a,b,c)=1$ (for $u=0$ this is $(0,0,1)$). For a point $Q$ of $E(K_0)$ put $\xi(Q)=1/x(Q)$ if $Q\ne O$ and $x(Q)\ne0$, and $\xi(Q)=0$ otherwise.

results.summary: There are exactly $66$ primes $p\le324$, and These are the two decimal literals of the saved specification. In binary, $P_s$ has $433$ digits and $W$ has $435$.

results.title: The finite false-triple product
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an integer $T\ge0$, a triple $(a,b,c)\in\mathbb Z^3$ is a false triple in the box if $|a|,|b|,|c|\le T$ and $ab\ne c$. For such a triple write the fifteen coordinates of $(\iota(a),\iota(b),\iota(c))$, in point-major order, as reduced fractions $A_j/B_j$ with $B_j>0$ ($j=1,\dots,15$), and put $D_{abc}=\prod_{j=1}^{15}B_j$.
